fieldDomains.form: a non-empty list of t("STR-KEY") values
fieldDomains.name: TextKeyList

fieldDomains.form: a non-empty list of Theme.Colors.<Token> values
fieldDomains.name: ColorTokenList

productions.name: screen
productions.note: The whole file is one screen. Its name is CamelCase; the recipe records the pairing with the lowercase artifact id rather than either being derived from the other.

productions.name: surface
productions.note: Optional. A file without one still parses and is still checked, but layout, overflow and golden bounds are not - mdux-medui-check reports that as MDC002 rather than passing quietly.

productions.name: component
productions.note: The component name must be one the dictionary carries, and its fields exactly the set that entry admits: every required one present, no unknown one. See components.

productions.name: row
productions.note: A single-level horizontal group, flattened at compile time. A Row inside a Row is refused rather than flattened, because the solver has no second axis to give it.

productions.name: annotation
productions.note: Precedes the node it annotates. @safety_critical(cv_check: [...]) is the one annotation with a rule attached: the node it marks must carry a requirement.

productions.name: value
productions.note: Which forms a field admits is the field's domain rather than the grammar's - see fieldDomains. Localizable text is always t("STR-KEY"): a literal in such a field is refused, because a screen carrying one locale's words is not locale-free.
productions.rule: value = pixels | "Fill" | number | string | text-key | image-ref | color-token | identifier | point | list ;

productions.name: screen-member
productions.note: A screen's body is these three in any order. `layout` and `surface` may each appear once; everything else is a node.

productions.name: layout
productions.note: The identifier is the layout kind - `Vertical` is the one the solver implements. The block carries `spacing` and `padding`, both sizes.

productions.name: node
productions.note: Annotations precede the component they mark, and there may be more than one.

productions.name: field
productions.note: One property per line by convention, and the sibling implementation requires it - it splits a component body on the first colon of each line. This parser is token-based and would accept several on one line, so writing one per line is what keeps a screen portable in both directions.

productions.name: pixels
productions.note: The only unit. `Fill` is the other size form and takes no number; there is no percentage, em or point.

productions.name: point
productions.note: What `position:` and `surface:` take. A lone `Npx` is a size; the comma is what makes it a point.

productions.name: list
productions.note: Used by `states:` and `colors:` on a StatusIndicator, which must pair one to one.

productions.name: text-key
productions.note: The only way to write localizable text. A literal in such a field is refused, because a compiled screen is locale-free and carries the key rather than the words.

productions.name: image-ref
productions.note: Names a baked image package by id. The screen approves that package's identity and intrinsic extent; no compressed bytes and no decoder reach a device.

productions.name: color-token
productions.note: Written `Theme.Colors.<Token>`, and validated against the governed table rather than against the shape - see themeTokens for the set. The parser keeps the dotted path whole and unresolved; semantic analysis is what refuses an unknown one.

productions.name: forbidden
productions.note: Absent by design rather than unimplemented. A screen whose shape depends on data is a screen whose worst case no compiler can measure, which is what every bound in this language rests on.
productions.rule: (* no production: loops, conditionals, recursion and scripting are absent *)
